title: Naval Communications Hardware Nomenclature Flashcards
description: Flashcards to rapidly master the official alphanumeric nomenclatures and hardware codes for Naval network routing, switching, cryptography, and tracking systems.

flashcards.back: The legacy Automated Digital Network System (ADNS) hardware variant that is currently being retired across the fleet.
The current Automated Digital Network System (ADNS) variant installed Afloat (shipboard) to route IP addresses and manage network enclaves.
The current Automated Digital Network System (ADNS) variant installed at Shore facilities (e.g., NCTAMS and NCTS) to terminate fleet IP connections.
Secure Audio Switch (SAS) housed in a bright red cabinet. Used electrically to switch and connect voice circuits to crypto interface units and red phones.
Tactical Variant Switch (TVS) designed to switch both digital and analog interfaces and establish secure voice conference calls aboard ships.
The standard physical RF patching panel. Colorkeyed RED for unsecure/decrypted/unencrypted paths, and BLACK for secure/encrypted paths.
The primary commercial/satellite RF modem (manufactured by Comtech EF Data) used on naval vessels for digital SATCOM data transmissions.
Multiplexer used to combine four individual incoming signals at a base data rate of 16 kbps each on UHF Demand Assigned Multiple Access (DAMA) satellite circuits.
Demultiplexer circuit device used to separate or 'break out' the multiple incoming composite signal streams for the Fleet Satellite Broadcast.
An upgraded cryptographic hardware device used to encrypt and decrypt tactical voice communications over VHF and UHF radio systems.
The Simple Key Loader (SKL). A handheld fill device used by technicians to securely store, transport, and load Cryptographic Keying Material (KEYMAT) into switches and crypto units.
The primary sensor for Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD). A multi-functional, phased-array radar that simultaneously searches, tracks, and guides interceptor missiles.
A massive, floating, mobile radar station housed under a large white dome. Designed to operate in extreme heavy seas to track long-range ballistic missile trajectories.
